product_overview: Pigeon is a desktop-first API client workspace for composing, sending, and organizing HTTP requests. It supports multi-tab request building, environment variables, history/drafts, collections, and cURL import/export in a single main view.
core_goals: Compose HTTP requests with methods, URL, query params, headers, auth, and body data
Send requests and inspect responses including status, headers, body, HTML preview, and SSE streams
Organize work across multiple request tabs, history, drafts, and saved collections
Reuse environment variables and built-in tokens across URLs, headers, and bodies
Import requests from cURL and export the current request back to cURL
Persist preferences such as theme, word wrap, and request options

features.name: Request Builder
features.description: Build and edit an HTTP request using the method picker, URL bar, query parameters, headers, auth, and body editors.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open a new request tab -> Select an HTTP method -> Enter a request URL -> Add query parameters and headers -> Switch between Params, Auth, Headers, and Body editors -> Enter request data -> See the composed request reflected in the workspace
Navigate to / -> Paste a curl command into the URL bar -> See the request populate with method, URL, headers, auth, body, and params -> Review and adjust the imported request
Navigate to / -> Enter a URL with query parameters -> Edit parameters in the Params editor -> See the URL update to stay in sync
Navigate to / -> Add many headers or long values -> Scroll within the editor area -> Continue editing without leaving the workspace

features.name: Send and Response Viewing
features.description: Execute the current request and inspect the returned response in the response panel.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Compose a valid request -> Send the request -> See the response status, body, timing, and size
Navigate to / -> Send a request that returns HTML -> Switch between preview and text views -> Inspect the rendered content
Navigate to / -> Send a request that returns JSON -> Switch between pretty and raw response views -> Review the formatted body
Navigate to / -> Start an SSE request -> Watch events appear in the live event list -> Stop the stream when finished
Navigate to / -> Toggle response word wrap -> See the response body reflow inside the panel

features.name: Tabbed Request Workspace
features.description: Work across multiple request tabs with actions to create, rename, duplicate, and close tabs.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open a new request tab -> Build a separate request in that tab -> Switch back and forth between tabs -> Keep each request state intact
Navigate to / -> Double-click a tab label -> Rename the tab inline -> Continue editing the request with the custom name preserved
Navigate to / -> Open the tab context menu -> Duplicate the current tab -> Edit the copy independently
Navigate to / -> Open the tab context menu -> Close the current tab or close other tabs -> Continue working in the remaining tab(s)

features.name: Collections
features.description: Save requests into nested collections and folders, then reopen them later from the sidebar tree.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Create a collection from the sidebar -> See the collection appear in the Collections tree
Navigate to / -> Open a request with a URL -> Save the active request to a chosen collection or folder -> Reopen it later from the tree
Navigate to / -> Create a folder inside a collection -> Add nested requests or folders -> Browse the saved tree structure
Navigate to / -> Rename or delete a collection, folder, or saved request -> Confirm the change -> See the tree update accordingly

features.name: Environments
features.description: Define environment variables and global variables, then insert them into requests with interpolation.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open the environment manager -> Create an environment -> Add variables -> Select it as the active environment
Navigate to / -> Enter {{var}} tokens in the URL, headers, or body -> See variable suggestions while typing -> Use the active environment value in the request
Navigate to / -> Switch to a different environment -> See the request use the new values when sent
Navigate to / -> Mark an environment as production -> Send a mutating request -> Confirm the production warning before proceeding

features.name: Import / Export cURL
features.description: Import requests from cURL commands and export the current request as cURL.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open the import drawer -> Paste a curl command -> Submit the import -> See a new request tab open with the imported request
Navigate to / -> Paste a curl command into the URL bar -> See the current request updated in place -> Continue editing the populated request
Navigate to / -> Build a request -> Export the current request as cURL -> Copy the generated command for use in a terminal or document
Navigate to / -> Try to import invalid curl text in the import drawer -> See the parse error and keep the current workspace unchanged

features.name: History and Drafts
features.description: Review previously sent requests and resume auto-saved working drafts from the sidebar.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Send a request -> Open the History tab -> See the request recorded with status and time
Navigate to / -> Edit a request without explicitly saving it -> Open the Drafts tab -> Resume the auto-saved draft
Navigate to / -> Click a history entry or draft entry -> Open that request in a tab -> Continue editing or resend it
Navigate to / -> Search within History or Drafts -> Filter the visible entries -> Clear the search to restore the full list

features.name: Settings
features.description: Adjust app preferences such as theme, word wrap, request behavior, and data management.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open Settings -> Switch between Dark and Light theme -> See the interface update and persist
Navigate to / -> Open Settings -> Toggle word wrap -> See body and response editors wrap or unwrap text consistently
Navigate to / -> Open Settings -> Change request options such as follow redirects, SSL verification, or proxy URL -> Send a request using the updated preferences
Navigate to / -> Open Settings -> Clear history, drafts, or all supported data -> Confirm the action -> See the selected data removed

routes.description: Single-view API client workspace (tab strip, sidebar, request builder, response viewer). No client-side router; all features render in one view.

features.name: Request Builder
features.description: Compose an HTTP request - method, URL, query params, headers, auth, and body.
user_interactions: Select HTTP method via method-trigger dropdown
Switch editor tabs (params, headers, auth, body)
Add/edit key-value rows for params and headers
Paste a curl command into the URL bar to auto-import

api_calls.endpoint: user-supplied URL (sent via Rust reqwest in desktop, fetch in browser)

features.name: Send / Execution
features.description: Send the composed request and view the HTTP response.
user_interactions: View response status, body, HTML preview

features.name: Tabs
features.description: Multiple request tabs with rename, duplicate, and close variants.
user_interactions: Double-click tab label to rename inline
Right-click tab for context menu (new/duplicate/close/close others/close all)

features.name: Collections
features.description: Save requests into a folder/request tree; create/rename/delete collections and folders.
user_interactions: Save active request via Cmd+S to a collection destination

features.name: Environments
features.description: Environment variables with interpolation into URL/headers/body.
user_interactions: Define variables and reference them with var-suggestion autocomplete

features.name: Import / Export
features.description: Import a request from a curl command, export request as curl.
user_interactions: Paste curl into import-curl-textarea and submit

features.name: History and Drafts
features.description: Persisted request history and auto-saved drafts.
user_interactions: Reopen a past request from history

features.name: Settings
features.description: Theme (dark/light), word-wrap, and request options (follow redirects, SSL verify, proxy).

known_limitations.issue: In the browser/dev build, the Tauri Rust backend is unavailable; persistence falls back to localStorage and HTTP send uses browser fetch (subject to CORS).
known_limitations.impact: Real SQLite persistence and CORS-free reqwest sending are only exercised in the packaged desktop app, not under browser-based testing.

known_limitations.issue: No authentication/login exists in the app.
known_limitations.impact: All features are reachable without login.
